A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Foresight work and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained material can be matched reliably despite appendix reorganization and added sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original generation-quality comparisons, inference profiling, hyperparameter ablations, and feature-variation analyses in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds newer-model comparisons, matched-quality speed measurements, cumulative timing, and a reported FLUX experiment.

M1.justification: The warmup procedure, MSE thresholds, cache updates, reuse decisions, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Appendix E.5 applies reuse to FLUX's spatial components without introducing a new decision procedure; Section 3.5 adds analysis rather than an implemented algorithm revision.

E1.justification: V2 adds PenguinVideoBenchmark evaluation and extends the evaluated task from text-to-video to FLUX text-to-image generation in Appendices E.2 and E.5. Existing VBench, Open-Sora, UCF-101, and EvalCrafter prompt coverage is retained.

E2.justification: TeaCache, cited but not evaluated in v1, becomes an actual comparator on HunyuanVideo and Wan-2.1 in v2 Table 8. Static, Delta-DiT, T-GATE, and PAB remain in their original comparisons.

E3.justification: V2 adds comparisons at matched PSNR, a separate 500-prompt cumulative-runtime measurement, and tests on 10 randomly sampled PenguinVideoBenchmark prompts using HunyuanVideo at 720p/2 seconds and Wan-2.1 at 480p/5 seconds. These substantially extend evaluation design; the original 550-prompt VBench protocol and baseline settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E.3 newly tests whether speed advantages persist when output similarity is matched to PAB, while E.1 supplements per-prompt latency with cumulative workload timing. Existing warmup, reuse-window, scaling-factor, and feature-variation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Latency ± values and Figure 7 error bars already appear in v1. V2 uses the same reporting practice for added results without introducing repeated-run counts, new seed protocols, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial results for HunyuanVideo/Wan-2.1, cumulative timing, and the FLUX extension. Table 9 newly reports matched-PSNR Foresight speedups of 1.68×, 1.58×, and 1.95× against PAB's 1.26×, 1.29×, and 1.37×. Original Table 1 scores, ablation values, and UCF-101/EvalCrafter results remain unchanged; these additions are not improvements to retained same-setting measurements.

T1.justification: New Section 3.5 introduces Equations 8–12, layerwise reuse-error bounds, Lipschitz and contraction assumptions, and an accumulated-error argument claiming preservation of convergence. V1 contains no corresponding convergence analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same main contribution: training-free adaptive layer reuse preserving video quality, up to 1.63× speedup on the original three models, and a threefold cache-memory reduction. Added evidence and theory do not revise these summary claims.

C2.justification: Appendix E.3 newly emphasizes parameter transfer without model-specific tuning and contrasts this with PAB and TeaCache. Section 5 additionally suggests finer-grained applicability. Its discussion of larger reuse windows or shorter warmup sacrificing quality largely repeats v1's existing ablation interpretation.

D1.justification: V2 reports TeaCache's 0.1 threshold and describes the components reused in FLUX, but abridges the disclosed Figure 6 prompt. Existing hardware information, sampling settings, baseline configuration tables, and code-access information remain unchanged; the matched-quality configurations are not fully specified.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for HunyuanVideo, Wan, and FLUX, and expands its positioning against PAB and TeaCache through the tuning discussion. The original related-work review is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: V2 adds convergence and limitations sections and reorganizes Appendix A.1–A.7 into thematic Appendices A–E with additional subsections. Most existing prose remains unchanged, so this is a limited structural refinement rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 8, 9, and 11 and expands Figure 15 with a cumulative-timing table. The original Table 8 becomes Table 10, Figure 6's caption is shortened, and retained material reflows. Original figure content is preserved. Table 11 is captioned Open-Sora despite its surrounding FLUX discussion.

improvement.justification: The newer-model and matched-quality comparisons usefully broaden v1's empirical support. However, Section 3.5 assumes reverse-process contractivity without establishing it for the evaluated models and describes perturbations as vanishing despite deriving a finite residual bound. The FLUX quality claim also lacks quality measurements, and Table 11 has conflicting attribution. Useful added evidence and new reliability concerns coexist, leaving the net quality effect uncertain.
